title: Audit Schema Versioning and Evidence Tagging Standard for Cross-Region Model Serving
author: Leila Morgan
body:
Overview
--------
This document defines Redwood Inference’s standard for audit event schema versioning and evidence tagging applied to cross-region model serving traffic (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to ensure all telemetry used for compliance evidence, incident response, and cross-border retention decisions is: consistent, discoverable, and backward-compatible.

Scope
-----
Applies to:
- Inference request/response audit logs emitted by runtime components (router, inference workers, cache, composer).
- Authorization and entitlement events (RBAC changes, API key lifecycle, role activations).
- Evidence artifacts produced for incident investigations (forensic snapshots, pseudo-anonymized payload pointers).
- Cross-region replication metadata and retention tags.

Out of scope: application-level business logs (customer application traces that are not proxied through Redwood runtime).

Principles
----------
1. Single source of truth: All audit-producing services must emit a canonical event envelope with standard header fields (see Event Header below).
2. Minimal required fields: Each event MUST contain the required fields; optional fields must be populated when available.
3. Versioning policy: Major.minor.patch semantic versioning for schema (v1.0.0). Minor/patch changes are backward-compatible; major changes require migration plan and cross-team sign-off.
4. Evidence tagging: Every event intended for compliance/forensics must carry evidence tags that drive retention and access controls.
5. Privacy-first: Sensitive payloads must never be stored in plain text. Use pointer-to-encrypted-artifact and retention tag rather than embedding PII.

Event Header (required fields)
-----------------------------
The canonical audit envelope is a JSON object emitted on the audit topic/stream. Required top-level fields (string values unless noted):
- event_id (UUID)
- emitted_at (ISO-8601 UTC timestamp)
- schema_version (string, e.g., "v1.2.0")
- source_service (string, e.g., "router", "inference-worker")
- environment (string, one of: "prod", "staging", "dev")
- tenant_id (string)
- request_id (UUID)
- model_id (string)
- model_version (string)
- deployment_mode (string, one of: "hosted", "dedicated", "private")
- geo (string, ISO country code where event was generated)
- severity (string, one of: "info","warning","error","security")
- evidence_tags (list of short strings)
- retention_policy_id (string)

Standard evidence_tags (recommended)
- "compliance:gdpr"
- "compliance:ccpa"
- "evidence:incident"
- "evidence:rbac-change"
- "sensitive:encrypted-pointer"
- "dataflow:cross-region-replicated"

Optional fields (populate when available)
- actor_id, actor_type (user/service/mobile/app)
- policy_snapshot_id (id of RBAC policy evaluated)
- auth_method (string, e.g., "jwt", "api_key", "oauth")
- kv_cache_key_hint (string)
- input_hash (sha256) and pseudo_anonymization_level (string)
- artifact_pointer (string URI to encrypted blob in evidence store)

Schema Versioning and Change Process
-----------------------------------
1. Versioning scheme: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Bump MAJOR for breaking changes (field renames/removals), MINOR for additive non-breaking changes, PATCH for documentation/formatting clarifications.
2. Proposal: Engineers submit a Schema Change Request (SCR) in the repo: infra/audit-schema/changes with a clear compatibility justification and migration plan.
3. Review: Security, Privacy, Platform Reliability (SRE), and Product must review SCRs. Target review window: 5 business days for MINOR/PATCH; 10 business days for MAJOR.
4. Migration: For MAJOR changes: a) dual-write mode (old+new schema) for at least 7 days in prod traffic, b) automated compatibility tests, c) evidence extraction tools must support both schemas for 90 days post-cutover.
5. Release: Tag schema in the schema registry and publish changelog. Update related docs and dashboards.

Retention Policy Mapping
------------------------
Retention decisions are derived from retention_policy_id on the event header. The default registry maps policy IDs to retention windows and allowed access scopes:
| policy_id | retention_days | access_level | cross_region_replicable | notes |
|-----------|----------------|--------------|-------------------------|-------|
| R-30     | 30             | security-team | no                      | short incident triage |
| R-365    | 365            | security+legal | yes                    | typical audit evidence |
| R-730    | 730            | legal-only    | conditional             | regulatory hold candidates |
| R-forever| indefinite     | legal-archival | restricted              | court/regs only (requires approval) |

Retention decision flow (high level):
1. Event emitted with retention_policy_id.
2. Ingestion pipeline tags the event and routes it to hot store or cold evidence store based on retention_days.
3. Cross-region replication is triggered if cross_region_replicable is true and tenant residency/geo rules allow it.
4. Automated retention jobs run daily to enforce deletion or archival; deletion requires evidence tombstone and audit record.

Evidence Tagging Use Cases
-------------------------
- Incident response: Tag events with "evidence:incident" and include artifact_pointer to forensic snapshot. Incident responders must be able to query by request_id, tenant_id, and model_version.
- RBAC audits: Tag with "evidence:rbac-change" and include policy_snapshot_id. Retain for 365 days by default.
- Cross-border compliance: If a tenant is geo-restricted, ingestion must override cross-region replication even if evidence tag suggests replication.

Operational Runbook (collecting audit evidence during an incident)
----------------------------------------------------------------
1. Triage: Pager duty response team creates an incident with ID (INC-YYYYMMDD-N).
2. Evidence freeze: Change retention_policy_id for related events to R-365 or R-730 (as required) using the Evidence Orchestration CLI.
   Example CLI:
   
   rwood-evidence set-policy --incident INC-20260910-3 --filter "tenant_id=acct-1234 AND emitted_at>2026-09-10T00:00:00Z" --policy R-365

3. Snapshot: Request artifact pointers for inference-worker memory dumps and save encrypted blobs to forensic store; tag events with "evidence:incident".
4. Access: Grant access through short-lived audit-role tokens (JIT) scoped to incident_id with expiry.
5. Post-incident: Record retention changes and generate evidence package manifest. All changes must be recorded in the evidence change log (EL-entries) and signed by incident owner.

Emergency rollback for schema release (on-call procedure)
--------------------------------------------------------
1. If consumers fail to parse the new schema, trigger rollback: set ingestion gate to accept only schema_version X.Y.Z-1 and enable dual-write backfill.
2. Notify teams via #sec-audit-alerts and create a runbook entry.
3. Revert producer library releases and increment PATCH in schema registry after fix.

Testing and Validation
----------------------
- Unit tests: enforce required fields present and types validated against JSON Schema.
- Contract tests: Producers must include contract-test suite; consumers run integration tests against a published schema mock.
- Canary: Schema consumer canary in prod receives 0.5% traffic; alert threshold: parsing error rate > 0.05% triggers rollback.
- Evidence completeness test: quarterly automated verification that every RBAC-change event has policy_snapshot_id and evidence_tags populated.

Dashboards and Alerts
---------------------
Essential dashboards:
- Schema parsing error rate (by service, by version). SLO: <0.05% per hour.
- Evidence tag coverage (percent of events with evidence_tags) by tenant and service. SLO: 99.5% daily coverage for RBAC and security-severity events.
- Cross-region replication failures (count, last 24h). Alert if > 10 failures per hour.

Owners and Roles
---------------
- Security (owner): schema governance, approval of MAJOR changes, incident oversight.
- Platform Infra: implements ingestion, dual-write, and schema registry.
- Runtime Engineering: updates producers and ensures event populations.
- Legal & Compliance: retention policy definitions and approval for R-forever designations.
- SRE: monitors dashboards and executes rollbacks.

Checklist for a Schema Change Request (SCR)
-----------------------------------------
1. SCR doc link and rationale.
2. Backward compatibility matrix.
3. Dual-write plan and duration.
4. Consumer impact list and owners.
5. Test plan (unit, contract, canary).
6. Evidence migration utilities if required.
7. Rollback criteria and comms plan.
8. Required approvers and sign-off.

Appendix A — JSON envelope example (v1.2.0)
-----------------------------------------
{
  "event_id": "7f3b8b8c-2d4a-4a1b-ae9a-5d6b7c8f9a1c",
  "emitted_at": "2026-09-12T14:22:11Z",
  "schema_version": "v1.2.0",
  "source_service": "inference-worker",
  "environment": "prod",
  "tenant_id": "acct-0a1b2c",
  "request_id": "b1e2f3c4-55d6-4a7b-9c01-23456789abcd",
  "model_id": "gptx-7b",
  "model_version": "2026-08-31-quantized",
  "deployment_mode": "dedicated",
  "geo": "GB",
  "severity": "security",
  "evidence_tags": ["evidence:incident", "sensitive:encrypted-pointer"],
  "retention_policy_id": "R-365",
  "artifact_pointer": "s3://forensic-store/enc/2026/09/12/7f3b8b8c"
}

Appendix B — Common failure scenarios and mitigations
-----------------------------------------------------
- Parsing errors in consumers: automated rollback and alert; patch consumer with tolerant parser.
- Missing retention_policy_id: ingestion defaults to R-30 and emits an op-telemetry alert for producer owner.
- Cross-region replication blocked by tenant residency: ingestion overrides replication and tags event with "dataflow:geo-blocked"; a compliance ticket is created for legal review.

Document maintenance
--------------------
This document is maintained by Security. Review cadence: annually, or on any MAJOR schema release. For questions or to request expedited review, ping @sec-schema in Slack or email sec-schema@redwood.ai.
